t.1.203.1: Then all the divine seers, the Siddhas and the supreme seers, seeing that great slaughter, fell into the deepest distress.
t.1.203.2: Then they, who had conquered anger, mastered themselves and subdued their senses, went to the abode of the Grandfather out of compassion for the world.
t.1.203.3: Then they saw the Grandfather seated together with the gods, surrounded on all sides by Siddhas and brahmarṣis.
t.1.203.6: Then all the great seers, approaching together, related in full the deeds of Sunda and Upasunda.
t.1.203.8: Then all the hosts of the gods, and those supreme seers as well, putting that very matter foremost, urged the Grandfather.
t.1.203.7: Then they reported everything in full to the Grandfather: what had been done, how it had been done, and in what order.
t.1.203.10: With the slaying of those two in mind, he summoned Viśvakarman; and on seeing Viśvakarman, the Grandfather of great austerity commanded him: "Let a woman be created here who will be desired by all."
t.1.203.9: Then the Grandfather, having heard those words of them all, pondered for a moment, as it were, the resolve as to what had to be done.
t.1.203.11: Having bowed to the Grandfather and welcomed his words, he reflected with great effort and fashioned a divine woman.
t.1.203.12: Whatever being there was in the three worlds, whether unmoving or moving, that was beautiful to behold, he diligently gathered each and every such thing from here and there.
t.1.203.4: There was the god Mahādeva, there was Agni together with Vāyu, the Moon and the Sun, and Dharma, Parameṣṭhin, and likewise Budha.
t.1.203.5: The Vaikhānasas, the Vālakhilyas, the Vānaprasthas, the Marīcipas, the Ajas and the Avimūḍhas, the Tejogarbhas and other ascetics, all these seers wait in worship upon the Grandfather.
t.1.203.13: And he set jewels by the millions into her body; thus he created her, fashioned of a mass of gems, divine in form.
t.1.203.14: Fashioned by Viśvakarman with great effort, she became unequalled in beauty among the women of the three worlds.
t.1.203.16: Like Śrī herself in embodied form, lovely of form and beautiful of body, she captivated the eyes and the minds of all beings.
t.1.203.15: There is not even the smallest part of her body that is not endowed with the richness of beauty, nor any place where the gaze of those beholding her does not cling.
t.1.203.17: Because she was fashioned by gathering together the jewels bit by bit, each a tiny sesame-seed's portion, the Grandfather therefore gave her the name Tilottamā.
t.1.203.18: Go, Tilottamā, to the two asuras Sunda and Upasunda, and with your desirable beauty, good lady, work their seduction.
t.1.203.20: Saying "So be it" in assent, she bowed to the Grandfather and there made a circle around the assembled gods, keeping them on her right.
t.1.203.19: Act in such a way that, merely from the sight of you and through the splendour of your beauty, enmity may arise between those two, one against the other, on your account.
t.1.203.21: The Blessed One sat facing east, with Maheśvara to the south; the gods were seated to the north, and the ṛṣis were gathered on every side.
t.1.203.22: While she was making her circumambulation of that assembly there, Indra and the blessed Sthāṇu held themselves firm with composure.
t.1.203.23: As he longed intensely to see her, when she then passed to his side, another face, its eyelashes curving at the tips, sprang forth on his right.
t.1.203.25: And for great Indra too, a thousand large eyes with reddened corners arose on every side, at his flanks, behind him and in front.
t.1.203.24: As she moved around behind him, a western face sprang forth; and when she went to his northern side, a northern face sprang forth.
t.1.203.26: Thus in former times Sthāṇu, the Great God, became four-faced, and likewise the slayer of Bala became thousand-eyed.
t.1.203.27: Likewise the faces of the hosts of gods and of the ṛṣis on every side turned toward wherever Tilottamā went.
t.1.203.28: The gaze of all those great-souled ones fell upon her body, for the most part, except for the god Pitāmaha.
t.1.203.29: Then, as she went about, all the gods and the supreme seers deemed that task as good as accomplished, because of the perfection of her beauty.
t.1.203.30: But when Tilottamā had then departed, the Creator of the worlds dismissed all the gods and those hosts of ṛṣis.
